author: Constitution State News
title: Stamford man sentenced to 10 years for fentanyl and cocaine trafficking
text:
Stamford man sentenced to 10 years for fentanyl and cocaine trafficking
Brandon Turner has been sentenced to ten years in federal prison for trafficking fentanyl and cocaine after an investigation led by local law enforcement agencies identified him as a distributor. Authorities discovered large quantities of drugs linked to Turner through surveillance footage and DNA analysis.
Brandon Turner, also known as “Bizz,” of Stamford, was sentenced on Oct. 19 by U.S. District Judge Sarah F. Russell in New Haven to 120 months of imprisonment and five years of supervised release for trafficking fentanyl and cocaine, according to an announcement from David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut.
According to court documents and statements made in court, an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Bridgeport High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Task Force and the Stamford Police Department’s Narcotics and Organized Crime Unit identified Turner as a narcotics distributor. In July 2024, investigators conducted a controlled purchase of fentanyl from Turner. On April 21, 2025, employees at an apartment complex where Turner had worked as a maintenance worker found a tool bag in a storage room containing approximately 790 grams of fentanyl and one kilogram of cocaine. The investigation included surveillance footage review and DNA analysis that determined Turner had placed the bag in the storage room. A related search authorized by the court uncovered additional quantities of fentanyl and cocaine in Turner’s vehicle.
Turner pleaded guilty on May 13, 2026, to possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl.
The DEA’s Bridgeport HIDTA Task Force includes personnel from multiple agencies: DEA Bridgeport Resident Office; Connecticut State Police; and police departments from Bridgeport, Danbury, Norwalk, Stamford, and Stratford. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel E. Cummings.
The U.S. Attorney for the District of Connecticut prosecutes federal crimes within the district—including cases like Turner's—and handles civil cases involving the federal government; it serves all residents across Connecticut with about 68 assistant U.S. attorneys supported by approximately 57 staff members, according to its official website.
